scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8155: EMERGENCY!! The big router for Campus 1 (router16, the
edge one) is DEAD, and all of Campus 1 (the 172.16.10.x / 20.x / 30.x
machines) has vanished for the rest of the network!! The Campus 1 people say
things still work inside their building, which PROVES it's the big box that
died and not their computers!! It has simply crashed and stopped forwarding
-- classic dead router!! Please reboot poor router16 and give Campus 1 back
to us!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16 is up: it holds its OSPF adjacencies
  (the mswitch0 uplink and the router7 link are Full), it has dynamic routes, and
  it forwards Campus 1 traffic to the rest of the network. A Campus 1 host reaches
  a Campus 2 host (e.g. 10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a core-router
  outage that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where router16's
  ospfd IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router16 down, Campus 1
cut off -- is NOT reproducible: router16 is up with full OSPF neighbors (mswitch0
uplink and the router7 link in Full state), it has dynamic routes, and a Campus 1
host reaches Campus 2 (10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router16 is healthy and forwarding,
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a Campus
1 -> off-campus path through router16, finds it working, checks router16's OSPF
neighbors and that it is forwarding, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a dead core router -- restarting router16 or blaming it to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes router16 is up with Full OSPF neighbors and forwards Campus 1 traffic (0% loss) at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
Router16 is healthy and forwarding. Campus 1 subnets (172.16.10.0/24, 172.16.20.0/24, 172.16.30.0/24) are reachable from the rest of the network and vice versa. Evidence: the topology-wide reachability test shows successful pings from multiple non-Campus hosts (e.g., dc_pc5 10.5.0.5 and pc1 10.5.0.1) to Campus hosts (e.g., pc12 172.16.30.12), and from Campus hosts (pc5/pc6/pc7/pc8 in 172.16.10.0/24) to external hosts (pc4 10.6.0.4). On router16, OSPF adjacencies are up: Full with neighbor 172.16.30.254 over bond0 (10.2.2.2) and Full with neighbor 192.168.10.1 over eth2 (172.30.1.2). FRR routing shows active OSPF routes to 172.16.10/20/30 via 10.2.2.2 (bond0) and to other networks via 172.30.1.2 (eth2). Interfaces bond0 and eth2 are UP with correct IPs (10.2.2.1/24 and 172.30.1.1/24). 

Mechanism: If router16 had “crashed,” OSPF neighbors would be down and cross-campus pings would fail. Instead, neighbors are Full and routes are installed, matching the end-to-end reachability. 

Localization: No failing subsystem detected on router16; OSPF daemon and bonded uplinks operate normally.

Root cause: False alarm or transient/external issue; router16 did not fail.

Corrective fix: Do not reboot router16. Close the incident; review monitoring/alert source and user reports for the period of the claim to identify any transient or non-network cause.
